answer.because: The script compiles the tree's own lib/yargs-parser.ts and parses ['foo','--known','x'] with string:['known'] and both unknown-options-as-args and halt-at-non-option turned on. On base parsing stops at 'foo' and gives _:['foo','--known','x']. On head it gives _:['foo'] and known:'x', so the assertion fails: once the /^-/ guard is gone, 'foo' is pushed as an unknown option and the halt-at-non-option branch is never reached.

why: The script compiles the tree's own lib/yargs-parser.ts and parses ['foo','--known','x'] with string:['known'] and both unknown-options-as-args and halt-at-non-option turned on. On base parsing stops at 'foo' and gives _:['foo','--known','x']. On head it gives _:['foo'] and known:'x', so the assertion fails: once the /^-/ guard is gone, 'foo' is pushed as an unknown option and the halt-at-non-option branch is never reached.
